AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To document spectrum of paediatric liver disorders confirmed on liver biopsy.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: The retrospective review of patients was conducted at Shifa International Hospital, Islamabad, Pakistan, and comprised data of all children who underwent ultrasound-guided percutaneous liver biopsy between December 2008 and June 2015. Frequency of individual diagnosis was assessed and compared on gender basis. SPSS 16 was used for statistical analysis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There were medical records of 74 patients in the study with an overall median age of 6.9 years (interquartile range: 0.2-17.7 years). Metabolic 27(36.5%) and inflammatory 19(25.6%) disorders were the most common aetiologies. At presentation 29(39.1%) patients had cirrhosis; and 25(34%) children were <5 years of age. Metabolic disorders were the most common aetiology in children upto 10 years of age with 19(25.6%) patients. Above the age of 10 years, inflammatory disorders were more frequent and were seen in 10(13.5%). Based on gender, a trend towards significance was observed for metabolic disorders (p=0.08) and children who presented with cirrhosis (p= 0.07), but it was not statistically significant.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Metabolic disorders were the most common cause of liver disorders. A number of children at presentation had underlying cirrhosis.
